design.tapMechanism:
MECHANISM: one uniform, three uniform-gated early returns inside planet-lod-lab.html's OWN fragment shader, and a readback that compiles that very string.

EXACT UNIFORM (insert in the lab fragment shader immediately AFTER planet-lod-lab.html:257, the `uniform float uRiverCarvePatchStrength;` line, before the patchDepth comment block):

      // ── AC-SAMPLER instrument tap. 0 = render (every branch below is dead); 1 = composite body;
      // 2 = solid surface (post-carve, pre-liquid); 3 = post-liquid. Uniform-gated early return, so
      // the taken path at 0 is unchanged token for token. The instrument compiles THIS string.
      uniform int uFieldTap;

EXACT TAPS (all inside the ANALYTIC branch, i.e. the else of `if (uNormalMode == 1)` at :370):

  TAP_COMPOSITE — insert after :397 (the `}` closing `if (uCraterBakeRestore > 0.0) {`), before `float h = hd.x;` at :398:
          if (uFieldTap == 1){ gl_FragColor = hd; return; }   // AC-SAMPLER tap: composited body, pre-combiner
  (hd is already vec4(h, grad) at that point, so this emits both channels with no re-packing.)

  TAP_SOLID — insert after :484 (the `}` closing `if (uRiverCarveStrength > 0.0){` at :462), before the Stage-4 comment at :485:
          if (uFieldTap == 2){ gl_FragColor = vec4(h, grad); return; }   // AC-SAMPLER tap: solid surface

  TAP_LIQUID — insert after :496 (the `}` closing `if (uSeaLevel > -1.0){` at :492), before the F20 comment at :497:
          if (uFieldTap == 3){ gl_FragColor = vec4(h, grad); return; }   // AC-SAMPLER tap: post-liquid surface

JS uniform (lab side, after planet-lod-lab.html:1466, next to uRiverCarvePatchStrength):
    uniforms.uFieldTap = { value: 0 };   // AC-SAMPLER instrument tap (0 = render)
Lab-side, NOT in planet-lod-uniforms.js makeUniforms: the router program never needs it, and an extra key on the shared uniforms object is ignored by materials that do not declare it.

HOW THE READBACK DRIVES IT. planet.material.uniforms IS the shared `uniforms` object (planet-lod-lab.html:1477), and window._lab already exposes both `planet` and `uniforms`. The sampler is constructed FROM THE MATERIAL, not from imported constants:

  fragmentShader: planetMaterial.fragmentShader      // the same JS string reference — no copy, no concat
  uniforms:       planetMaterial.uniforms            // asserted === the lab's uniforms object
  vertexShader:   deriveTapVertex(planetMaterial.vertexShader)

deriveTapVertex is three substitutions on the planet's own vertex source, each asserted to match EXACTLY ONCE (throw otherwise), plus one prepended attribute:
  prepend  `attribute vec3 aDir;`
  `vPos = position;`                        -> `vPos = normalize(aDir);`
  `vObjN = normalize(position);`            -> `vObjN = normalize(aDir);`
  `gl_Position = projectionMatrix * modelViewMatrix * vec4(position, 1.0);`
                                            -> `gl_Position = vec4(position.xy, 0.0, 1.0); gl_PointSize = 1.0;`
Everything else — vBand/vShear/vMush/vStorm plumbing, vSubstellarAngle from uLightDir — comes along unchanged, so a varying added lab-side appears in the tap program automatically instead of silently going missing. A point-cloud readback cannot use a perspective vertex shader; this is the minimum irreducible divergence and it is derived, not authored.

createHeightSampler (planet-lod-rivers.js:431) gains three OPTIONAL params, all defaulting to today's values so every existing caller is byte-inert:
  fragmentShader = HEIGHT_FRAG, vertexShader = HEIGHT_VERT, extraAttributes = {}
extraAttributes allocates zero-filled BufferAttributes ({ aBand:1, aShear:1, aMush:1, aStorm:1 }) so the point geometry satisfies the lab vertex shader's attribute set. read() gains a tapPoint argument; it sets uniforms.uFieldTap.value = tapPoint alongside the existing uOctaves/uFwClamp pins and restores all three in a finally block. It refuses (throws) when uNormalMode.value === 1 or uDebugMode.value !== 0, because in those states the tapped locals either do not exist or are never reached.

WHY THIS IS NOT A DUPLICATED PROGRAM. The fragment source is the planet's own string object; `instrumentMaterial.fragmentShader === planet.material.fragmentShader` is checkable with ===, and a headless fence test fails if fieldSampler.js ever mentions HEIGHT_FRAG or ROUTER_MAIN again. The only new GLSL anywhere is four lines of tap and one uniform declaration, all of which the planet itself carries.
design.inertnessArgument:
THE CLAIM. With uFieldTap == 0 no tap branch is taken, so the surviving path executes the identical sequence of expressions on identical inputs; the edit reads one uniform and writes gl_FragColor only inside branches that are not entered. Nothing before or between the taps is re-ordered, re-typed, or re-scoped: the inserts sit between statements, declare no variable, and shadow nothing. The three branch conditions are dynamically uniform across the draw, so there is no divergence and no derivative-in-divergent-flow hazard — which matters, because the analytic branch calls fwidth (:376, and inside ecuRelief at planet-lod-height.glsl.js:2802) and textureCube both before and after the tap points.

WHY IT IS A CLAIM AND NOT A THEOREM. Source-level equivalence does not imply bit-level equivalence after a driver's optimiser. Introducing control flow can change register allocation and spilling, can inhibit or enable hoisting/sinking of a texture fetch or a common subexpression, and — the one that actually bites — can change which multiply-add pairs get contracted into an FMA. GLSL leaves FMA contraction and intermediate precision to the implementation. A single ULP shift in h propagates through smoothstep edges (the F14 liquidMask band, the F20 shore SDF, the relief gate) and through the Stage-6 posterize split, so a 1-ULP arithmetic change can become a 1/255 pixel change at a threshold crossing.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT — the test working-Claude runs, not an axiom I get to assert:
  Fixed camera, fixed seed, fixed preset, uFieldTap = 0. Capture PNG A on HEAD (edit absent), apply the edit, capture PNG B. Compare byte-wise (sha256 of the decoded pixel buffer, not the PNG container). Repeat on Rocky (Earthlike) at the camera floor AND at a far stop (different uOctaves loop trip counts, different branch mix), plus one gas preset (uBandStrength > 0, a different Stage-6 path). Any differing pixel falsifies "byte-inert".
  Note there is NO automated net for this: golden 40c18aad cannot see relief (it hashes a motion accumulator), and fence-baseline.json / l0-baseline.json are CPU relief artifacts that never run the fragment shader. The capture pair IS the net, and it belongs in the workstream directory as an artifact.

FALLBACK LADDER IF IT FAILS, so a red result is a decision and not a dead end:
  (i) Quantify: count differing pixels and max per-channel delta. Bisect by applying one tap at a time — three separate inserts means three separate suspects.
  (ii) If the difference is bounded (e.g. <= 1/255 on threshold-adjacent pixels), DECLARE it with the measurement in the workstream record rather than claiming inertness. An honest measured bound is worth more than a false axiom, and this workstream's whole complaint is about confident wrong numbers.
  (iii) If it is larger, restructure: collapse to a single tap point (TAP_SOLID only) and recover the composite anchor by other means, or gate the entire analytic block. Do not proceed on an unexamined difference.

SECOND-ORDER INERTNESS RISK, separate from the compiler: uFieldTap is a live uniform on the material the planet renders with. If it is ever left nonzero — an exception between set and restore, a second writer, a paused frame loop — the planet renders raw float field data as colour. Mitigation: the set/restore pair brackets a single synchronous renderer.render() with no awaits inside, restore lives in finally, and the fence test asserts the lab source contains exactly one write of uFieldTap.value outside the sampler.
design.octaveDecision:
DECISION: pin. The grid read keeps uOctaves = 9 and uFwClamp = 0 (unchanged from today's sampler), records the live values in every sample's metadata, and exposes the viewport tap as a declared secondary mode. I am not eliminating the tradeoff; I am choosing a side and stating the bill.

WHY PIN.
1. Every consumer needs a field that is a function of the body, not of the camera. AC-MEASURE's observable is "the readout tracks radius when the slider moves" — an unpinned instrument would also track where Max happens to be flying, and the two effects are not separable in the number. AC-HYPSO's dip test, modal separation and area fractions are all octave-sensitive. AC-ONEBODY compares the router's field to the renderer's, and the router routes at octaves 9; comparing across different LODs would manufacture a difference that is not the one the AC is about.
2. autoOctaves (planet-lod-lab-core.js:24) returns mix(4, 9, lodRamp). Pinning at 9 is not an arbitrary LOD — it is the MAXIMUM the renderer ever displays, reached at the camera floor. The measurement is the rendered field at the renderer's own highest detail.
3. The screen-space fade is not reproducible in the grid path at all, so "measure the live frame's octaves" is not on the menu there. fwidth over a 1-texel point primitive is 0 (user varyings are constant across a point), so fwBase is 0 regardless. Every consumer of fwBase in the shader sits behind `if (uFwClamp == 1)` — verified across fbmd:772, fbmdRidged:1000, fbmdHetero:2177, fbmdDamped:2208, ecuRelief:2810 — so pinning uFwClamp = 0 makes that dead value provably unused rather than silently garbage. Pretending a point RTT reproduces a per-pixel fade would be the same class of fiction as the km axis this module's header already refuses.

WHAT IS LOST, stated rather than argued away.
  a. Fine-scale vertical statistics — RMS relief at small scales, slope percentiles, the high end of the spectral slope — are an UPPER BOUND on what any single frame shows, because the read carries octaves 0..8 at full weight with no sub-pixel fade while a given frame at a given distance may carry fewer octaves and fades the finest ones. Continental-scale statistics (hypsometry, modal separation, mountain-belt relief, the km figure AC-MEASURE wants) live far below that band and are unaffected.
  b. The read is not the pixels on screen. It is the same PROGRAM at a declared LOD, evaluated at directions we choose. Field identity is about the chain and the composite, not about per-pixel LOD.
  c. Camera dependence that survives INSIDE the field is inherited, not neutralised: uRiverCarvePatchN/U/V is the tributary-patch centre and is literally the camera direction (planet-lod-lab.html:3972-3978), and uLodRamp is read inside facetCombiner (planet-lod-height.glsl.js:2579) and ecuRelief (:2803). Both are inert at today's defaults (uRiverCarvePatchStrength 0; facet/ecu coverage 0 on the tectonic presets) but they are real, they are in the rendered field, and neutralising them would restore exactly the defect AC-SAMPLER exists to close. They are recorded per sample and reported when nonzero.

WHAT REPLACES THE LOST INFORMATION. The viewport tap: render the planet's own mesh with its own vertex shader and the live camera into a float target with uFieldTap = 2, uFwClamp restored to 1, uOctaves at the live value. That path has the true camera-dependent octaves and the true screen-space fade — it is the literal displayed field — at the cost of camera-determined, area-non-uniform, non-reproducible sampling that no global descriptor can use. It runs as control leg L5 and reports a NUMBER (fadeGap) for how far the pinned read sits from the current frame, instead of an assertion that it does not matter.
design.gradientHandling:
Both channels are emitted at every tap and both are asserted on, at two independent points, with a live mutation test that proves the gradient legs discriminate.

EMISSION. TAP_COMPOSITE emits `hd` directly — hd is already vec4(h, grad) at :397, so the composite's height and its baked gradient go out together with no re-packing and no opportunity to substitute. TAP_SOLID and TAP_LIQUID emit vec4(h, grad) with the running accumulator. `gradBase` (declared at :402 as hd.yzw for massWastCombiner's F19 trick) is never referenced by any tap.

WHY ROUND 2 COULD NOT SEE THE SUBSTITUTION, and why this can. Round 2's legs were differences of two configurations of the FINAL height; the gradient channel was never read by any leg, so vec4(h, gradBase) passed everything. Here the gradient is load-bearing in two legs that are not differences of configurations:

  L2 (composite anchor). At TAP_COMPOSITE with uReliefBakeStrength = 1 and uCraterBakeRestore = 0, the emitted vec4 must equal the baked relief cube's own RGBA at the sample direction — R = height, GBA = the tangent-plane gradient the cube was baked with (planet-lod-tectonic.js:322 writes exactly vec4(vHeight, vGrad.xyz)). This is an ABSOLUTE comparison of the emitted gradient against CPU-side data, in ONE configuration. Substituting anything for the gradient channel, or dropping the baked gradient from the composite (round-2 counterexample 3), fails on the GBA channels directly.

  L4 (gradient/derivative consistency). At TAP_SOLID the emitted grad is checked against a numerical derivative of the emitted h. Sample directions are shipped in ε-triplets: for each probe direction d with orthonormal tangents t1, t2, also sample normalize(d ± ε t1) and normalize(d ± ε t2) at ε = 2e-3 rad. Central differences give dh/ds along each tangent; the prediction is P·grad where P = I − dd^T, because vPos is unit-length (R = 1.0 at planet-lod-lab.html:198, and the tap vertex shader sets vPos = normalize(aDir)), so an arc-length step of ε along t moves position by ε t + O(ε²). Statistic: least-squares regression of the finite difference on the predicted directional derivative, pooled over probes and both tangents; require slope ≈ 1 and R² above a calibrated floor.
  Under gradBase substitution the emitted grad is ∇(composite) while the finite difference of the emitted h contains ∇(composite) + Σ_k ∇g_k. The residual is exactly Σ_k ∇g_k, which is large: gradient variance is dominated by the fine octaves and by the ridged mountain/crater/scarp terms, not by the 256³ cube. Slope stays near 1 (the base gradient is a genuine component) but R² collapses — which is why the leg reads R², not slope alone.

CALIBRATING L4's FLOOR HONESTLY. Some combiner gradients in this codebase are chain-rule approximations, and two terms are knowingly inconsistent by construction: the AC4 carve scales the height drop by uRiverCarveDepth and the gradient bend by uRiverCarveStrength (:483-484), and the F14 cut neglects the gradient of liquidMask itself (:493-495). So the correct implementation has a nonzero residual too. Floor calibration, not guesswork: run L4 at TAP_COMPOSITE first, where the relation is exact because both channels come from one cube fetch — that measures the readback + finite-difference noise floor. Then run at TAP_SOLID, and require the gradBase mutant's R² to sit clearly below the true implementation's. If the separation is not clear, L4 has lost power and must be reported as such rather than passed.

MUTATION TEST — the leg proves itself, live, without editing any file:
  const mut = planet.material.fragmentShader.replace('if (uFieldTap == 2){ gl_FragColor = vec4(h, grad); return; }',
                                                     'if (uFieldTap == 2){ gl_FragColor = vec4(h, gradBase); return; }');
  assert exactly one occurrence replaced; compile mut into a throwaway material with the same derived vertex shader and the same uniforms; read; run L4. Assert L4 FAILS on the mutant and PASSES on the real material. The mutant is never used for measurement, is not a re-implementation of the chain (it is a one-token substitution on the live string), and is disposed immediately.

control.approach: Not plant-and-difference on the final field. Three mechanisms, none of which the cancellation lemma touches: (1) STRUCTURAL IDENTITY — the instrument compiles the planet material's own fragmentShader string reference and binds its own uniforms object, so 'which chain ran' is settled by === on program text, not by argument; (2) ABSOLUTE ANCHORING — the composite tap is compared against independently-obtained CPU-side cube data in a SINGLE configuration, so there is no second evaluation for terms to cancel against; (3) PER-TERM COEFFICIENT PLANTS — where differencing is used, the plant is each term's OWN gating uniform, so the lemma's hypothesis (d g_k / d u = 0) fails by construction for the term under test. Plus one CROSS-OBSERVABLE leg (emitted gradient versus numerical derivative of emitted height), which subtracts two different observables of one configuration rather than two configurations. Explicit statement of why the lemma does not apply: the round-2 lemma says that for d(x) = h_A(x) - h_B(x) differing only in a planted uniform u, every g_k with dg_k/du = 0 cancels term for term. L1 is not a function of field values at all. L2 and L4 form no difference of two chain evaluations. L3 sets u := the coefficient of g_k itself, so dg_k/du != 0 for the term under test and it cannot cancel. L3's one differencing leg that IS lemma-shaped -- TAP_SOLID minus TAP_COMPOSITE -- cancels exactly the composite terms, and those are precisely the terms L2 covers absolutely: the two legs partition the chain, prefix by absolute anchor, suffix by difference, with no gap.
control.whyNotBlind: Counterexample 1, the program running only base + mountains + lava + carve with 20 of 26 combiners absent: IMPOSSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION, and separately caught. Impossible, because such a program is a different string from planet.material.fragmentShader, and L1 asserts reference identity before any number is produced -- there is no longer a place to put a reduced program. If someone were to reduce the LAB'S OWN shader instead, then that reduced field is what the planet renders and the sampler is correct by AC-SAMPLER's own wording (the defect would be a terrain regression, visible in the render). Separately caught anyway by L3: each of the absent combiners' live gates would fail to move TAP_SOLID, and L3 reports per-gate coverage rather than a pass/fail aggregate, so it names which ones went dead. Counterexample 2, both taps emitting vec4(h, gradBase) instead of vec4(h, grad): NOT caught by L1 (the substitution lives inside the shared string and the planet never executes the tap), and this is exactly the residual surface the technique creates. Caught by L4: the emitted gradient is regressed against the central-difference derivative of the emitted height on epsilon-triplet probes, and under substitution the unexplained residual is exactly the sum of the combiner gradients, which dominate gradient variance at octave 9. Proven red, not assumed: the control builds the mutant by one-token string substitution on the live fragmentShader, compiles it, and asserts L4 fails on it and passes on the real one. Also caught at the composite point by L2's GBA channels. Counterexample 3, the baked gradient dropped from both cube composites: caught twice. L2 compares TAP_COMPOSITE's GBA channels against the cube's own baked gradient texels absolutely -- a dropped gradient reads as zeros against nonzero cube data. And structurally, dropping the baked gradient changes what perturbAnalytic receives at :550, so it changes the rendered planet: it is a terrain bug the render itself displays, not a measurement error hiding behind an instrument.

legs.name: L1 SOURCE AND UNIFORM IDENTITY (structural; live assert + headless fence)
legs.asserts: Live: instrumentMaterial.fragmentShader === planet.material.fragmentShader (reference identity, plus sha256 recorded) and instrumentMaterial.uniforms === planet.material.uniforms. Headless (tests/instrument-tap-fence.test.js): the lab fragment shader contains exactly the three tap statements verbatim, each immediately following its named anchor (the uCraterBakeRestore block, the uRiverCarveStrength block, the uSeaLevel block); no other gl_FragColor write or return exists in the analytic branch; uniform int uFieldTap is declared exactly once and defaults to 0 exactly once lab-side; fieldSampler.js contains no reference to HEIGHT_FRAG or ROUTER_MAIN; the three deriveTapVertex substitution targets each occur exactly once in the lab vertex shader.
legs.catchesWhat: Any reduced, extended, paraphrased or stale copy of the height program -- the entire round-2 failure class. Also catches the sampler silently reverting to its own program, a tap being moved or deleted, an extra early return being added, and the vertex derivation losing its anchors.
legs.redToday: YES. fieldSampler.js:57 imports createHeightSampler, which hardcodes fragmentShader: HEIGHT_FRAG (planet-lod-rivers.js:448) = HEIGHT_GLSL + ROUTER_MAIN. That is a different string from the lab's fragmentShader, so the identity assert fails today, and every headless clause fails today because no tap exists.

legs.name: L2 COMPOSITE ANCHOR (absolute, single configuration, both channels)
legs.asserts: At the live default (uReliefBakeStrength = 1, so uCraterBakeRestore = 0), TAP_COMPOSITE's emitted vec4 must reproduce the baked relief cube at the sample direction: R against the cube's height texel, GBA against the cube's baked gradient texels. Preferred exact form: sample at cube TEXEL CENTRES, where bilinear filtering returns the texel value and the face/uv convention reduces to an index, and read the cube back per face via readRenderTargetPixels. Fallback if the HalfFloat readback type is not supported by the driver: regress against the CPU carrier field the cube was baked from (buildHeightCubeGeometry's aHeight/aGrad), requiring slope ~ 1 and R^2 above a tolerance derived from half-float quantisation (~5e-5 absolute at h ~ 0.1) plus cube-texel angular size (90/256 deg) versus carrier mesh spacing.
legs.catchesWhat: The measured body not being the baked body -- the literal AC-SAMPLER defect. The dropped-baked-gradient counterexample, via the GBA channels. A tap-A misplacement (if it sat after mountainCombiner the equality breaks). Any substitution in the composite tap's emission.
legs.redToday: YES, and this is the AC's own indictment. Today's sampler renders ROUTER_MAIN, whose h begins at fbmd(vPos, uOctaves, 0.0) with no cube fetch anywhere, while the lab's live default is uReliefBakeStrength = 1, a pure baked body. Regressed against the cube, today's field gives R^2 near zero.

legs.name: L3 PER-TERM SENSITIVITY AND INVARIANCE (plant in each term's OWN coefficient; byte-exact, threshold-free)
legs.asserts: For each gating uniform that is LIVE (nonzero) in the tested configuration -- every combiner amplitude/coverage gate, uSeaLevel, uRiverCarveStrength/Depth, the fluvial and outflow gates -- perturb it, re-read, restore, and require the TAP_SOLID (or TAP_LIQUID for uSeaLevel) readback to differ in bytes; and require the TAP_COMPOSITE readback to be byte-IDENTICAL. Conversely, uReliefBakeStrength, uCraterBakeRestore, and a planted edit in the baked cube must move TAP_COMPOSITE. GPU evaluation of one program on identical inputs is deterministic within a session, so the criterion is exact byte equality, not a threshold. Output is a per-gate coverage table, not an aggregate pass.
legs.catchesWhat: Missing or dead combiners, individually and by name -- the counterexample-1 class, caught per-term rather than in bulk. A tap placed too early in the chain (later gates stop moving it). A tap-A that is not actually the composite (a combiner gate would move it). The router/renderer body split at the heart of AC-SAMPLER (bake-strength insensitivity).
legs.redToday: YES, on the terms that matter most. Today's ROUTER_MAIN field does not move when uReliefBakeStrength, uCraterBakeRestore, uSeaLevel, the F11 fluvial gate or the AC4 carve gates move -- ROUTER_MAIN has no cube fetch, no fluvialCombiner and no F14 cut. It does move for most other combiner gates (ROUTER_MAIN carries them), so the leg is honest about partial overlap: it is red exactly where the defect is, and its per-gate table says so.

legs.name: L4 GRADIENT VERSUS DERIVATIVE (cross-observable, single configuration, mutation-tested)
legs.asserts: Regress the central-difference derivative of the emitted h (epsilon-triplet probes at eps = 2e-3 rad along two tangents) on the predicted directional derivative from the emitted grad projected into the tangent plane. Require slope ~ 1 and R^2 above a floor calibrated at TAP_COMPOSITE, where the relation is exact because both channels come from one cube fetch. Then compile a one-token string mutant of the live shader (vec4(h, grad) -> vec4(h, gradBase) at TAP_SOLID), assert exactly one replacement, and require the leg to FAIL on the mutant while passing on the real material.
legs.catchesWhat: The gradBase-for-grad substitution that killed round 2, and any other wrong-variable emission in the gradient channel. Also flags a tap whose h and grad come from different points in the chain.
legs.redToday: RED BY UNAVAILABILITY. There is no gradient-emitting tap in the rendered program today, so the observable cannot be produced and the leg errors out. Its load-bearing property is not the status quo but the named adversary: it is proven red against the gradBase mutant by the live mutation, which is the threat that actually defeated round 2. Stated plainly so it is not mistaken for a leg that discriminates against today's sampler on its own -- today's ROUTER_MAIN emits an internally consistent (h, grad) pair for its own chain and would pass this leg while failing L1, L2 and L3.

legs.name: L5 VERTEX-PLUMBING PARITY AND FADE GAP (viewport tap versus grid tap)
legs.asserts: Render the planet's own mesh, own vertex shader and live camera into a float target with uFieldTap = 2 and uFwClamp = 0. Ray-cast the camera through each sampled pixel to the unit sphere (R = 1.0, planet-lod-lab.html:198) to recover its direction, feed those exact directions to the grid sampler, and require agreement within a tolerance derived from the 256x256 tessellation chord error (interpolated vPos is short of unit length by ~theta^2/8, theta = pi/256, i.e. ~1.9e-5 relative). Then re-run with uFwClamp = 1 and the live uOctaves and report the difference as fadeGap -- a measured number, not an assertion.
legs.catchesWhat: Divergence between the derived tap vertex shader and the planet's -- wrong vPos convention, a geometry radius that is not 1, a varying that turns out to reach h/grad, a missing attribute defaulting to something other than the lab's zeros. This is the ONLY leg that tests the one place where duplication is physically unavoidable. Second job: it quantifies what pinning octaves and disabling the sub-pixel fade actually costs, so the octave decision is reported with a number attached.
legs.redToday: RED BY UNAVAILABILITY (no tap exists, so there is no viewport field to compare). Load-bearing against shim drift, which is the residual risk the technique itself introduces; a hand-written vertex shim with vPos = aDir un-normalised, or a geometry radius other than 1, fails it immediately.

control.ciHome: Two homes, split by what can run without a GPU. (1) HEADLESS, tests/instrument-tap-fence.test.js, new file, runs in the standard suite: every L1 clause -- tap statements present verbatim at their named anchors, no other early return in the analytic branch, uFieldTap declared once and defaulted to 0 once, fieldSampler.js free of HEIGHT_FRAG/ROUTER_MAIN, the three deriveTapVertex substitution targets each occurring exactly once. If a future session moves a tap, deletes one, adds another early return, reverts the sampler to its own program, or reshapes the lab vertex shader, that named test fails instead of the instrument silently going back to measuring bare fbmd. The file must PASS on landing so the suite baseline stays at EXACTLY 4 named failures (GalacticFeatures x1, KnownObjects x3) = 17 failed FILES. It adds no /* glsl */ marker and no visScaleOf/sVis/VIS_SCALE_EXP token, so tests/vis-scale-fence.test.js is unaffected -- its two count assertions are over uDispDomainScale patterns only, which the edit does not touch. (2) LIVE, window._lab.tapControl(): runs L2 through L5 plus the mutation test in one call and returns a JSON verdict including the per-gate coverage table, the R^2 figures, fadeGap, and the recorded env (uOctaves live vs pinned, uLodRamp, uRiverCarvePatchStrength/N). Working-Claude drives it via chrome-devtools during the verify-workstream live integration step and stores the verdict plus the before/after inertness capture pair as artifacts under docs/WORKSTREAMS/world-engine-tectonic-realism-2026-07-29/. The live half cannot live in CI -- there is no GPU there -- so the headless half is deliberately the structural half: it guards the thing that would regress silently between sessions, while the value legs guard the thing a human is present for.

design.dissolvedBlockers:
DISSOLVED BY CONSTRUCTION — these cannot recur under this technique:

1. "INSTRUMENT_FRAG = HEIGHT_GLSL + INSTRUMENT_MAIN cannot compile: uRiverCarveMap, uRiverCarveStrength/Depth/Rough/GateHi, patchDepth() and sampleCarve() are lab-local." Gone. There is no second fragment program to assemble. The instrument compiles planet.material.fragmentShader, which is the lab's own self-contained string with those uniforms and functions declared in it. The concat that could not compile does not exist.

2. "The proposed CI parity region EXCLUDED the continuous bake blend (:381-393) and the crater restore (:394-397)." Gone. There is no parity region, because there is nothing to keep in parity: identity is === on one string. Both terms are inside the tapped chain by construction, and TAP_COMPOSITE sits immediately after the crater restore precisely so those two terms have an absolute anchor rather than a textual promise.

3. "The NEUTRALISE_LIST was incomplete on its own derivation rule — fluvialCombiner:1056, outflowCombiner:1130 and sublimationCombiner:2880 also read h, and outflow is live on Rocky at uOutflowDensity 0.30-0.45, which would have broken the arithmetic legs by ~8x." Gone. Nothing is neutralised. Every h-reading combiner runs exactly as the planet runs it, and their h-dependence is now a property of the measured field rather than a threat to the control, because L3 plants in each term's own coefficient instead of relying on an arithmetic decomposition that h-reading terms violate.

4. The cancellation lemma itself. L1 is not a function of field values. L2 and L4 form no difference of two chain evaluations. L3's plant is the term's own gate, so dg_k/du != 0 for the term under test. The one lemma-shaped leg (TAP_SOLID minus TAP_COMPOSITE) cancels exactly the composite terms, which are precisely the terms L2 anchors absolutely — prefix and suffix, no gap.

5. Round-2 counterexamples 1 and 3 (missing combiners; dropped baked gradient) stop being constructible as measurement errors. Counterexample 1 is a different program string, rejected by L1 before a number exists. Counterexample 3 changes what perturbAnalytic receives and so changes the render — it becomes a visible terrain bug rather than an invisible instrument bug, and L2's GBA channels catch it anyway.

STILL TO ANSWER — the technique's own bill, not inherited:

A. BYTE-INERTNESS IS NOW A LIVE RISK. Round 2 could not perturb the planet, because a separate program cannot. This edit is inside the program the planet renders, so "the instrument changed the render" is newly possible. This is the trade the technique makes: certainty about field identity bought with uncertainty about non-interference. Answered by the before/after byte-comparison at two camera distances on two presets, plus the declared fallback ladder — and by the fact that no automated net exists for it (golden 40c18aad cannot see relief; the CPU relief baselines never run the fragment shader), so the capture pair is the net.

B. THE OCTAVE/FADE QUESTION (round-2 B3). Unchanged and genuine. Answered by pinning at 9, declaring what that costs, and measuring fadeGap rather than asserting it away.

C. CAMERA DEPENDENCE INSIDE THE FIELD. Round 2 named uRiverCarvePatchN (patch centre = camera direction) as an undeclared third camera dependence. It is still there, and this technique makes it MORE real, not less: the tap reads the rendered field, so the dependence is inherited by design. A fourth exists that round 2 did not name — uLodRamp is read inside facetCombiner (planet-lod-height.glsl.js:2579) and ecuRelief (:2803), so camera distance enters the field, not just the shading. Both are inert at today's defaults and both are recorded per sample. They must be checked live per preset, not assumed.

D. THE VERTEX SIDE IS STILL NOT THE PLANET'S OWN. A point-cloud readback cannot use a perspective vertex shader. Answered by derivation-with-assertions plus L5 empirically, not by argument.

E. uNormalMode == 1. The finite-diff production path has no h/grad locals; the tap covers the analytic path only. The sampler throws there. AC-EXAG explicitly needs both paths compared (they disagree by ~24x today), so that comparison needs its own mechanism and does not come free with this tap.

F. GAS PRESETS. aBand/aShear/aMush/aStorm are zeros in the tap geometry and non-zero on the planet for gas presets. Verified by inspection that no varying other than vPos/vObjN is read before the tap points, but that is a grep result on today's source, which is why L1's headless clause pins the varying set and the derivation asserts its substitution targets.
residualRisks: Compiler-induced 1-ULP drift. Adding uniform-gated branches can change register allocation, expression sinking, or FMA contraction, and a 1-ULP shift in h can cross a smoothstep edge (F14 liquidMask, F20 shore SDF, the carve relief gate) or a posterize bucket and become a 1/255 pixel change. Falsifiable by the before/after byte comparison; if it fires, the honest move is to measure and declare the bound, not to re-argue inertness.

L2's exact form may not be available. The relief cube is HalfFloatType (planet-lod-tectonic.js:304); readRenderTargetPixels on a half-float cube face depends on the driver's implementation colour read type. If exact texel readback is unavailable, L2 degrades from an equality to a regression against the CPU carrier the cube was baked from, and its tolerance absorbs rasterisation plus bilinear plus half-float quantisation. Still red today by a wide margin, but no longer threshold-free.

L4's floor may not separate cleanly. Two terms in the shipped chain are knowingly gradient-inconsistent by construction: the AC4 carve scales height by uRiverCarveDepth and gradient by uRiverCarveStrength (planet-lod-lab.html:483-484), and the F14 cut neglects the gradient of liquidMask itself (:493-495). If the correct implementation's residual is not clearly below the gradBase mutant's, L4 loses discriminating power and must be reported as weak rather than passed. Mitigation is calibrating the floor at TAP_COMPOSITE, where the relation is exact.

L3 coverage is configuration-scoped, and saying otherwise would be the same overclaim this workstream keeps hitting. Combiners gated to zero in the tested preset (hexCrust, machineRelief, ecuRelief, shatter, chaos, cryoRidge on Rocky) contribute nothing to that configuration's field and cannot be exercised there. The leg reports the covered set per preset and must be run on at least Rocky plus one shell/volcanic preset; it never claims completeness.

L5's tolerance floor is set by the 256x256 tessellation chord error (~1.9e-5 relative on vPos), so a real vertex-plumbing divergence smaller than that is invisible to it. Tightenable by restricting comparison pixels to rays landing near mesh vertices, at the cost of sample count.

uFieldTap is a live uniform on the material the planet renders with. An exception between set and restore, or a second writer, leaves the planet rendering raw float field data as colour. Mitigated by a finally-block restore around one synchronous render and a headless assertion that exactly one write of uFieldTap.value exists outside the sampler — but the failure mode is loud and visible, not silent, which is the right shape.

The mutation test creates a throwaway material from a string-substituted copy of the live shader. That is one token, derived, never used for measurement, and disposed — but it is a program that is not the planet's, so it must never be reachable from the measurement path. The headless fence should assert the mutant construction lives only inside tapControl.

Line-number drift. The inserts push planet-lod-lab.html line numbers below :257 by about +9. No test pins a lab line number (checked across tests/), but the contract, intent and several source comments cite them, and stale citations are how a future session ends up reading the wrong block.

The technique settles WHICH FIELD is measured; it settles nothing about whether that field is right. AC-SAMPLER closing does not make the numbers physical — the vertical axis is still uncalibrated until AC-KMUNIT lands, and fieldSampler's existing refusal to emit km must stay in force until then.

attacks.breakAttempt:
ATTEMPT: construct a configuration that passes every control leg while the sampler measures a field the planet never renders — the round-2 failure class, reproduced against round 3. SUCCEEDED, under the design's own declared run plan.

The configuration: any tidally-locked preset (DRIVER_PRESETS carries 'Eyeball (locked temperate)' and 'Hot Jupiter (locked giant)', tests/feature-associations.test.js:16) with uFrostLocked==1 and uSubStrength>0 or uGlacialStrength>0. The derived tap vertex shader computes vSubstellarAngle from `position` (planet-lod-lab.html:223), which the derivation has redefined to the NDC readback-grid slot, so sublimationCombiner (planet-lod-height.glsl.js:2865, reads it at :2871) and glacialCombiner (:2949, reads it at :2954) write h and grad using a substellar angle keyed to the sample's texture index. Both run at planet-lod-lab.html:429-430, before TAP_SOLID at :484.

Leg by leg: L1 PASSES — the fragment string is byte-identical to planet.material.fragmentShader, and the three named vertex substitution targets each occur exactly once at :220, :221, :224, before and after. L2 PASSES — TAP_COMPOSITE sits at :397, before every combiner, so the corruption is not in the composited body at all. L3 PASSES and, worse, reports FALSE COVERAGE — perturbing uSubStrength or uGlacialStrength still moves TAP_SOLID in bytes (the wrong field is still gate-sensitive), so the per-gate table marks both combiners "covered" while the value they contribute is garbage. L4 WOULD fire (the epsilon-triplet probes land on different grid slots, so vSubstellarAngle differs wildly between a probe and its neighbours and the finite differences blow up) — but the design calibrates L4's floor on Rocky and residualRisks names the run set as "Rocky plus one shell/volcanic preset"; neither is locked, so L4 is never exercised on the breaking configuration. L5 WOULD fire for the same reason (its viewport leg uses the planet's own vertex shader, which gets vSubstellarAngle right) — and is likewise never run on a locked preset under the stated plan.

SO THE FIX IS TWO PARTS, NOT ONE. (a) Substitute the vSubstellarAngle line too, or better, assert the derived vertex source contains no occurrence of the token `position` outside the single gl_Position write — that is the invariant, and it closes against the next varying that keys on position rather than against this one. (b) Mandate L4 and L5 on a locked preset, because the two legs that CAN see vertex-plumbing corruption are exactly the two the current run plan never points at it.
